narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the existence of other installment plans. Your checking account balance in the 0-200 DM range was the most important reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, nearly 60% had no checking account at all and only 18% fell into your exact bracket; this limited positive balance signaled higher risk to the model and strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit.

Your credit history of critical or other existing credits was the second most influential factor. This actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval, because the bank has seen many customers with similar histories ultimately repay successfully. However, this positive influence was not large enough to overcome the other concerns.

Finally, the fact that you have an existing installment plan with a bank was the third most important driver. This detail increased the perceived risk and added further weight toward denial.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that the risk was too high. To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on building a stronger checking account balance and consider paying down or consolidating your existing installment obligations before reapplying.
